# growth-layer-reference — the REVIEWED inventory of growth surfaces the checked-in SSOT
# (scripts/growth-coverage.conf) must classify. One relative path per line; a trailing `.jsonl`
# or `.log` names an append-only FILE, everything else a DIRECTORY.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: tests/growth-coverage-lint.bats used to assert the SSOT against the LIVE
# ~/.claude layer. That is not a gate-able input — it is shared, concurrently-mutating machine
# state. `autonomy/cc-reaper.sweep.lock.d` is the proof: bin/cc-reaper mkdir-locks it for the
# duration of every sweep, so the same assertion passed and failed minutes apart on an unchanged
# tree. A land gate whose verdict depends on whether a cron job happens to be mid-sweep is a coin
# flip, and a flaky gate teaches people to re-run until green.
#
# WHAT IS PRESERVED: the bats assertion still checks real SSOT-vs-reference parity — a surface
# added here without a disposition fails the gate — and the reaper-claim leg still greps the
# BRANCH's own bin/ hooks/ scripts/, which is deterministic and is where a renamed reaper shows up.
#
# WHAT MOVED: "does the SSOT still describe the REAL host?" is now the nightly's job, not the
# gate's. scripts/growth-coverage-lint.sh with no GROWTH_ROOT override still reads ~/.claude, and
# the nightly `scripts/*lint*.sh` glob still runs it — a real live drift is caught there, where the
# answer is actionable and a red does not block an unrelated land.
#
# REGENERATE (after reviewing every added line — this is a reviewed artifact, not a dump):
#   G=~/.claude; { for d in "$G"/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] && basename "$d"; done
#     for d in "$G"/autonomy/*/; do [ -d "$d" ] && echo "autonomy/$(basename "$d")"; done
#     for f in "$G"/*.jsonl "$G"/*.log "$G"/autonomy/*.jsonl "$G"/autonomy/*.log; do
#       [ -f "$f" ] && echo "${f#"$G"/}"; done; } | sort -u
#
# Snapshot taken 2026-07-25 (infra-perfection wave), 85 surfaces, 0 unclassified against the SSOT.
# Re-snapshot 2026-08-10 (item c0ed177a12f7): +29 surfaces the live layer grew AFTER that audit.
# The nightly had been reporting them as unclassified against the SSOT; each was traced to its
# writer and to a deletion site (or the proven absence of one) before being classified, per the
# "reviewed artifact, not a dump" rule above. 114 surfaces, 0 unclassified against the SSOT.
